'''Bohemian knotweed''' is a [[nothospecies]] that is a cross between [[Japanese knotweed]] and [[giant knotweed]]. It has been documented as occurring in the wild in Japan.<ref name=mndoa>{{cite web |title=Bohemian Knotweed {{!}} Minnesota Department of Agriculture |url=https://www.mda.state.mn.us/bohemian-knotweed |website=www.mda.state.mn.us |access-date=18 October 2022 |language=en}}</ref> The scientific name is accepted to be '''''Reynoutria'' × ''bohemica''''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Reynoutria ×bohemica Chrtek & Chrtková |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/4038485 |website=www.gbif.org |access-date=24 October 2022 |language=en}}</ref> but it may also be referred to as '''''Fallopia'' × ''bohemica''''' and '''''Polygonum'' × ''bohemicum'''''.<ref name="cabi">{{cite web |title=Fallopia x bohemica |url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/108332 |website=www.cabi.org |access-date=24 October 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

The species was first described by {{ill|Jindřich Chrtek|es}} and {{ill|Anna Chrtková|cy}} in the [[Czech Republic]] in 1983.<ref name="cabi"/>

==Description==
The species is an herbaceous perennial that can spread through seeds and [[rhizome]]s. It can exceed 3.5 meters in height. Leaves are larger than those of Japanese knotweed, and leaf bases are less squared. White flowers typically open in August.<ref name="cabi"/> The species can be verified by the hairs along the mid-vein on the undersides of leaves, which are of different shape and texture than those found on either parent species.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hybrid knotweed (Bohemian knotweed) identification and control |url=https://kingcounty.gov/services/environment/animals-and-plants/noxious-weeds/weed-identification/invasive-knotweeds/bohemian-knotweed.aspx |access-date=24 October 2022}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Bohemian knotweed is typically found in riparian areas and waste places.<ref name="cabi"/> From the late 1800s, knotweeds have been introduced to new areas as an ornamental garden plant.<ref name=mndoa/>

The species has a worldwide distribution. It is considered by some as being a native hybrid of Japan.<ref name=mndoa/> In Europe, it has been reported from the British Isles, Germany, France, northern Italy, Serbia, Bulgaria, Belgium, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Romania, Ukraine, Scandinavia, and Switzerland. It is widespread in North America, and it has been discovered in Chile. It has also been found in Australia.<ref name="cabi"/>

==Management==
In some areas, Bohemian knotweed is classified as an invasive species and a noxious weed. It is illegal to transport and sell in multiple US states, including Minnesota,<ref name=mndoa/> Washington,<ref>{{cite web |title=Washington State Noxious Weed Control Board |url=https://www.nwcb.wa.gov/weeds/bohemian-knotweed |website=www.nwcb.wa.gov |access-date=24 October 2022}}</ref> and Wisconsin.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bohemian knotweed {{!}} (Fallopia x bohemicum or F. x bohemica or Polygonum x bohemicum) {{!}} Wisconsin DNR |url=https://dnr.wisconsin.gov/topic/Invasives/fact/BohemianKnotweed.html |website=dnr.wisconsin.gov |access-date=24 October 2022}}</ref>

Mechanical control and hand pulling are ineffective. Repeat herbicide application through spraying leaves and injecting stems is the best method.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bohemian Knotweed |url=https://www.invasivespeciescentre.ca/invasive-species/meet-the-species/invasive-plants/bohemian-knotweed/ |website=Invasive Species Centre |access-date=24 October 2022 |language=en-CA}}</ref> The beetle ''[[Gallerucida nigromaculata]]'' has been considered to have potential as a biological control.<ref name="cabi"/>
